changes.description: Initial desktop release
Fixed the system tray menu (right-click) on Windows
Only one backup agent can run per machine; a second launch now shows a clear notice
Automatic updates: in-app download of new versions with verification and release history
Version management, release manifests and CI template
Release builds and the app are named EverBox (everbox.exe, EverBox.app, everbox packages)

Security hardening: update downloads pinned to the manifest host over https, random per-download temp folder, queue replay re-validated against the job folder, https-only endpoints, keychain quoting hardened, log sanitizer covers 40-char secrets
Restore execution: agent downloads restore operations to a local folder (conflict policies, crash-safe writes, cancel); honest SSE copy (no more end-to-end claims)
Settings: restore destination folder picker; History: failed/ignored files listed on partial runs
Updates: the version shown in Settings follows CHANGELOG.json, new versions are checked on the public GitHub release repository, and updates can be installed automatically or manually
Update probe compatibility: manifests served over loopback http are accepted for the local dev/test transport (remote http stays refused)

Release notes: the release repository feed (version + description) is viewable in Settings, and the update notification carries what's new; one-command publishing organizes the release repository at every build
Fix build failure after the file_picker 13 upgrade: directory and save dialogs now use the new static API
Fixed: EverBox no longer shows a black window at startup on macOS — data is now stored inside the App Sandbox container and outbound network access is enabled
Rename upload throttle setting to 'Upload speed' (Mbps = network capacity) instead of 'Bandwidth' to remove ambiguity with data transfer quotas
Online storage card with quota and remaining space, clean History/Activity/Backups when connecting with new credentials, automatic updates now stop the app, install and relaunch
Backups page: remove a backup job from the row menu (confirmation dialog; files already backed up stay in the bucket)
Advanced > Device: show the actual app version and the real last synchronization time
Sign in with Everabyte: browser sign-in (OAuth PKCE), automatic device registration with backup-device quota, periodic device heartbeat
Release pipeline: real multi-OS CI packaging (Windows Inno installer, macOS signed+notarized DMG, Linux deb), latest.json stays atomic
Windows VSS: point-in-time volume snapshots for locked files (engine-level VolumeSnapshotProvider, no OS knowledge in backup_core); crash-recovery and snapshot tests; multi-OS field testing plan
Linux multi-format publishing: .deb + .rpm + AppImage auto-detected and published together, download page offers every format
Auto-update channel migrated to GitHub Releases (the raw latest.json feed was removed from the release repository — checks, downloads and silent auto-installs work again)
Update fallback button opens the everabyte.com downloads page instead of the GitHub repository
Sign-in with Everabyte fixed: API endpoint moves to api.everabyte.io and the browser consent page opens on app.everabyte.com/auth/agent (the old app.everabyte.io host no longer resolves)
Enrollment tokens (company deployments): paste an organization enrollment token on the Connect screen — the device registers and receives its own key (browser sign-in is now individual accounts only)
Connect screen: clear guidance for company accounts (API key or enrollment token instead of browser sign-in)

Recovery Radar: recovery readiness on the dashboard (recommended recovery point, verification state, measured restore estimate), alert banner on detected mass-change incidents, and aggregate recovery signals reported on each backup run
